ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circular sector diagram, with the gray shaded part occupying three-fourths of the circle; the uncolored part in the upper right is the discarded one-fourth circle, and its outer boundary is represented by a dashed arc. In the figure, a radius from the center of the circle to the circumference is labeled 4 inches. Reasoning: What the problem asks for is the dashed part, that is, the arc length of the discarded one-fourth circle. The radius r = 4, so the circumference of the whole circle is 2πr = 2π(4) = 8π. The arc length of the one-fourth circle is 1/4 of the circumference of the whole circle, so the arc length is (1/4)(8π) = 2π.

method.method_draft: Direct fraction-of-circumference route: First read the diagram as a circle sector picture where the gray/shaded paper is three quarters of a circle and the dotted arc is the unshaded discarded quarter. Read the radius label on the radius as 4 inches. From the text, confirm that the shaded part is a three-quarter circle of radius 4 and that the requested length is the dotted arc of the discarded quarter-circle. Use the rule that a quarter-circle arc is one fourth of the full circumference: arc length = (1/4)(2πr). Substitute r = 4 to get (1/4)(8π) = 2π.
